Phone MCP turns this phone into a server that AI assistants (MCP clients) can connect to. The app has no AI built in — you connect your own, for example Claude Code or Claude Desktop.
1. Enable the tools you want to expose. 2. Start the server with the toggle. 3. Connect your AI client — remotely through phonemcp.ai (works from anywhere), or over the same Wi-Fi network.
The connection guide on the main screen walks you through both.

It works — your AI has used a phone tool
1. Keep the server running and wait for the remote connection. If it stays disconnected, check internet access and allow background battery use below.
2. Choose your AI client below, follow its setup steps, then enter a pairing code. This screen updates automatically.
3. Enable the Sensors tool in the tool list, then paste this prompt into your AI client. Success appears here after an actual tool response.
Use phone_sensor to read my phone sensors. Tell me which sensors are available and explain one reading. Do not guess if the phone cannot be reached.
Try another useful task: enable Files, choose a folder you want to share, then ask your AI to find a document. You control which tools and files are accessible.
List the files I have shared from my phone. Ask me which document to read before opening it.
No tools in your AI client? Enable a tool in this app, reconnect the client and check its phone connection. A pairing code connects the client; the prompt tests the tool.
Keep using your phone tools from any network after the trial with a subscription. Monthly and yearly plans renew automatically until canceled in Google Play. Local Wi-Fi stays free.
